steps.message:
The fix is in place and the build passes. Here's a summary of the fix:

## Bug Analysis

**Root Cause**: In `TagsHelper.removeTag()`, the method used `replaceAll(tagToRemove.getText(), "")` which replaces **all** occurrences of the tag text as a substring, not just the specific tag token.

**Example**: If a note contains `#test #testa #testb` and the user unchecks `#test`, the buggy code replaced every occurrence of the substring `"#test"` — which matched inside `#testa` and `#testb`, incorrectly stripping them to just `#`.

## Fix

Changed the `removeTag` method in `TagsHelper.java` to use a word-boundary-aware regex pattern:

**Before (buggy):**
```java
title = title.replaceAll(tagToRemove.getText(), "");
content = content.replaceAll(tagToRemove.getText(), "");
```

**After (fixed):**
```java
String escapedText = Pattern.quote(tagToRemove.getText());
String tagPattern = "(?<!\\S)" + escapedText + "\\b";
title = title.replaceAll(tagPattern, "");
content = content.replaceAll(tagPattern, "");
```

The fix uses:
1. **`Pattern.quote()`** — escapes any regex special characters in the tag text (e.g., `#`, `.`, etc.)
2. **`(?<!\S)`** — negative lookbehind ensuring the tag is preceded by whitespace or is at the start of the string (i.e., it's a standalone whitespace-delimited token)
3. **`\b`** — word boundary at the end, ensuring we don't match partial tags like `#testa` when looking for `#test`
